headline: Trump says the ceasefire with Iran is over

sources.title: At NATO summit in Turkey, Trump says he believes ceasefire with Iran is over
Trump says ceasefire with Iran is 'over' as NATO summit wraps
Trump says ceasefire 'over', re-ups threats after US and Iran trade attacks

chunks.text: As a NATO [[summit]] {{wrapped up}} in Ankara, Turkey, U.S. President Trump told reporters that he believes the [[ceasefire]] with Iran is 'over.' The deal, signed only three weeks earlier, had promised peace. Trump said he [[no longer]] wanted to deal with Iran's leaders. His words {{set off}} worry among the [[allies]] who had [[gathered]], because a wider conflict could [[spread]] across the region.

verbs.correct: To come to an end or finish

verbs.wrong: To spread quickly from person to person
verbs.correct: To cause something to begin or happen suddenly

chunks.text: The trouble {{broke out}} after Iran attacked three commercial [[vessels]] in the Strait of Hormuz. This [[narrow]] [[strait]] carries about one-fifth of the world's oil. U.S. Central Command then {{stepped up}} its response and struck more than 80 [[targets]] in Iran. Iran's Revolutionary Guard {{hit back}}, firing missiles and drones toward Kuwait and Bahrain, two countries that [[host]] American military bases.

chunks.text: Trump did not fully {{rule out}} future talks, but he said that trying to negotiate with Iran was '[[a waste of time]].' At the same time, [[neither side]] seemed ready to {{back down}}. Officials {{pointed out}} that Trump had also [[threatened]] a naval [[blockade]], while his own negotiators still hoped to {{carry on}} with diplomacy.

chunks.text: Many people at the summit were unsettled by the news, and oil prices [[climbed]] soon after the fighting. The Gulf Cooperation Council {{spoke out}} against Iran's attacks, calling them a breach of international law. Trump also [[complained]] that several European nations had {{turned him down}} when he asked for more help. Even so, some diplomats still hoped to {{come up with}} a new deal and [[restore]] the [[truce]].

tf.s: Iran hit back at Kuwait and Bahrain by firing missiles and drones.
tf.why: Hit back means to respond to an attack, which is what Iran did against the two countries that host American bases.

tf.s: Some diplomats hoped to rule out a new deal to restore the truce.
tf.why: The diplomats hoped to come up with a new deal (think one up). Rule out means to decide something will not happen, the opposite of what they wanted.

tf.s: Trump complained that several European nations had carried on when he asked them for more help.
tf.why: Several European nations turned Trump down (refused his request). Carry on means to continue doing something, which does not describe refusing to help.

tf.s: As the NATO summit wrapped up in Ankara, Trump said he believes the ceasefire with Iran is over.
tf.why: Wrap up means to finish or come to an end, which the NATO summit did.

tf.s: After Iran's attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, the United States backed down.
tf.why: The United States stepped up its response and struck more than 80 targets. Back down means to stop demanding or arguing for something, which is not what the United States did.

tf.s: Fighting broke out after Iran attacked three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.
tf.why: Break out means to start suddenly, which is what the fighting did after the attacks on the ships.

mainIdea.s: The American president says the ceasefire with Iran is over after attacks on ships led to strikes from both sides. Allies now fear a wider conflict spreading across the region.
mainIdea.why: The truce collapsed after vessels were attacked in a key strait, and both militaries struck targets. Leaders at the summit were worried.

mainIdea.s: The White House has called negotiating with Iran a waste of time and fully closed the door on talks. A naval blockade of Iran's coast has begun and oil routes are already cut.
mainIdea.why: Close, but he did not fully rule out future talks, and the blockade was only a threat. His negotiators still hoped to carry on.

mainIdea.s: Oil prices are climbing around the world because a narrow shipping lane has been closed to all traffic. Countries are hunting for safer routes to move their tankers and cargo.
mainIdea.why: The strait was not closed. Prices climbed because of the fighting, but the story is about the end of the truce.
